summary: Otto Karow worked in Sinology, Japanology, and Tibetology, studying at Giessen, Leipzig, Humboldt University of Berlin, and Bonn (PD). He held positions at Bonn (1947), Münster (1951–1957), and Goethe University Frankfurt as professor of East Asian Philology (1960–1978).

Otto Loth specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer around 1863–1866 and served at the University of Leipzig from circa 1874 to 1881.

Otto Maenchen-Helfen worked in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. After studying at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig (Ph.D. under August Conrady), he held posts at the Marx-Engels Institute, Berlin, Mills College, and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).

Otto Rosenberg specialized in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at Saint Petersburg under Theodore Stcherbatsky and Sergey Oldenburg, and at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He taught at Saint Petersburg State University from 1911 to 1919.

Otto Schlaginhaufen earned his Ph.D. at the University of Zurich in 1905. He worked at the Rudolf-Virchow-Sammlung, the Museum of Ethnology in Dresden, and the University of Zurich, serving there as ordinary professor of anthropology from 1917 to 1950.

Otto Schrader specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at Jena, Berlin, and Leipzig (Ph.D.). He served as Oberlehrer at Carolo-Alexandrinum Jena (1877–1909), associate professor at Jena (1890), and ordinary professor of Indogermanistik at Breslau from 1909.

Otto Spies worked in religious studies and Indology, completing a Ph.D. under Enno Littmann at Tübingen and a Dr. juris at Bonn. He held professorships at Aligarh Muslim University (1932–1936), Breslau (1936), and Bonn (1951–1971).

Otto Stein worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Charles University (Dr. phil.) and the German University in Prague under Moriz Winternitz and Heinrich Swoboda, later serving as professor of Indology at the German University in Prague (1930–1939).

Otto Strauss was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Munich, Berlin, and Kiel (Ph.D. under Hermann Oldenberg). He held academic posts at Kiel, served as professor at the University of Calcutta (1913–1920), and at Breslau (1928–1935).
Otto Stursberg specialized in Indology and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the Humboldt University of Berlin between circa 1902 and 1907 under the supervision of Richard Pischel.
Otto Walter was an Indology scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Strasbourg around 1899–1903 under the supervision of Ernst Leumann.

Otto Wecker specialized in Indology, studying at Humboldt University of Berlin, University of Münster, and University of Tübingen, where he earned his Ph.D. under Richard von Garbe. He later taught at the University of Göttingen from 1947 to 1953.

Otto von Böhtlingk worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Saint Petersburg, Berlin, and Bonn under Bopp, Schlegel, and Lassen. He served at the Saint Petersburg Academy of Sciences (director 1849–1868) and the University of Jena (circa 1868–1885).

Otton Ottonovič Rozenberg worked in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Saint Petersburg (Ph.D.), Bonn under Hermann Jacobi, and Berlin under Rudolf Lange. In 1919, he served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.
Owen Flanagan is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fordham University and Boston University before becoming Professor of Philosophy at Duke University around 1996.

Owen Lattimore worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. He attended St Bees School, studied at Harvard University from 1928 to 1929, and held a post at the University of Leeds from circa 1963 to 1970.

P. A. Payutto is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who earned a bachelor's degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (~1957–1962). He served there as Associate Dean (~1964–1973) and became Tipitaka Acharaya at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1995.
P. Anujan Achan specialized in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and served as Government Archaeologist at the Thrissur Zoo and State Museum.
P. B. Meegaskumbura is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who served as a professor at the University of Peradeniya, with his post attested in 1991 and 2010.

P. D. Premasiri studied at Peradeniya, Cambridge, and Hawaiʻi (Ph.D. under Eliot Deutsch). Working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he served on the faculty at Peradeniya, where he headed the Pali and Buddhist Studies Department from 1997 to 2004.
